failure_mode: One positively-opening NC contact fails to open when ESTOP-01 is pressed, leaving either CH-A or CH-B in the healthy/on state.
local_effect: One demand channel changes to demand/off and the other remains healthy/on.
system_effect: CTRL-01 should recognize the demand from the channel that opened, de-energize Q1/Q2 and achieve the safe state; the channel discrepancy remains as a degraded fault and reset should be inhibited.
hazardous_consequence: No immediate hazardous consequence is expected for this single fault if the remaining channel and both de-energization paths operate; the loss of one input channel reduces fault tolerance for a later fault.
detection_mechanism: CH-A/CH-B discrepancy monitoring on the demand and the blocked reset required by SR-003 and SR-004.
recommended_action: Inject the fault separately on each contact, confirm Q1/Q2 de-energization, record the discrepancy time and verify that reset remains blocked until the fault is cleared.
assumptions: The unaffected E-stop contact and its input path operate as specified.
missing_information: ESTOP-01 contact failure data and the implemented CTRL-01 discrepancy logic are not supplied.

failure_mode: A common mechanical failure of ESTOP-01 prevents both positively-opening NC contacts from opening when the pushbutton is pressed.
local_effect: CH-A and CH-B both remain healthy/on despite the E-stop demand.
system_effect: CTRL-01 receives no demanded-state input, so Q1/Q2 and K1/K2 can remain energized/closed and SF-01 is lost.
hazardous_consequence: Power enabling hazardous robot motion can remain present while a person relies on ESTOP-01 to stop the motion.
detection_mechanism: No in-system detection mechanism for simultaneous stuck-healthy channels is identified in the supplied evidence; a two-channel demand test could reveal the failure.
recommended_action: Include a controlled common-mechanism demand test and obtain the pushbutton construction and validation evidence needed to assess this failure.
assumptions: A physically credible common mechanism can prevent both assumed positively-opening contacts from changing state.
missing_information: ESTOP-01 mechanical design, installation details and common-cause evidence are not supplied.

failure_mode: One NC contact opens without an E-stop demand.
local_effect: Either CH-A or CH-B changes to demand/off while the other channel remains healthy/on.
system_effect: CTRL-01 should treat the single-channel change as a demand, de-energize Q1/Q2, open K1/K2 and inhibit reset because of the discrepancy.
hazardous_consequence: The defined safe state is reached; the supplied boundary supports an unintended stop and loss of availability, not continued hazardous motion.
detection_mechanism: Demand-state recognition, CH-A/CH-B discrepancy monitoring and reset inhibition.
recommended_action: Perform a no-demand single-contact opening test and verify safe-state entry, diagnostic-state labeling and blocked reset.
missing_information: Consequences of an unintended robot stop outside the defined boundary are unknown.

failure_mode: An open circuit occurs in one E-stop input-channel wire.
local_effect: The affected NC input changes from healthy/on to demand/off independently of ESTOP-01 actuation.
system_effect: CTRL-01 should de-energize Q1/Q2, achieve the safe state, log a discrepancy and inhibit reset until the wiring fault is cleared.
hazardous_consequence: The defined safe state is reached; the immediate effect is an unintended stop rather than loss of SF-01.
detection_mechanism: Single-channel demand recognition plus the open-circuit/discrepancy monitoring required by SR-003 and SR-004.
recommended_action: Open each field wire individually and verify safe-state entry, diagnostic indication and reset inhibition.
assumptions: The 24 V NC input changes to demand/off when its field wire is opened.
missing_information: Input circuit topology and actual open-circuit diagnostic implementation are not supplied.

failure_mode: One E-stop input-channel wire is shorted to 24 V and remains healthy/on when its ESTOP-01 contact opens.
local_effect: The affected channel is stuck healthy while the other channel changes to demand/off.
system_effect: The unaffected channel should still cause Q1/Q2 to de-energize; the stuck-healthy channel creates a discrepancy that should be detected no later than the demand and should block reset.
hazardous_consequence: No immediate hazardous consequence is expected for this single fault if the unaffected input channel and output paths operate; input redundancy is degraded.
detection_mechanism: CH-A/CH-B discrepancy monitoring and the fault-injection behavior required by SR-003 and SR-004.
recommended_action: Apply a controlled short-to-24 V separately to each channel, demand the E-stop and verify safe-state entry, fault detection and blocked reset.
assumptions: The other input channel remains electrically independent and reaches demand/off.
missing_information: Input test-pulse arrangement, thresholds and diagnostic timing are not supplied.

failure_mode: A common field-wiring fault holds both CH-A and CH-B at 24 V during an E-stop demand.
local_effect: Both controller inputs remain healthy/on although both ESTOP-01 contacts have opened.
system_effect: CTRL-01 receives no demand, Q1/Q2 remain energized and K1/K2 remain closed, causing complete loss of SF-01.
hazardous_consequence: Power enabling hazardous robot motion can remain present during the E-stop demand.
detection_mechanism: No effective detection is established by the supplied evidence when both inputs remain mutually consistent in the healthy/on state; a common-fault injection test could expose it.
recommended_action: Review the actual input schematic and routing for credible common 24 V connections, then include the applicable common-fault injection in the fault matrix.
assumptions: A common 24 V source can reach both input lines downstream of the E-stop contacts.
missing_information: The field-wiring schematic, segregation and input diagnostic circuitry are not supplied.

failure_mode: A cross-fault electrically couples CH-A and CH-B without independently forcing either channel to demand/off.
local_effect: The two channels can change together and a single contact or wiring fault can be masked as a mutually consistent state.
system_effect: A normal two-contact E-stop demand may still de-energize Q1/Q2, but channel independence and discrepancy detection are degraded; whether the cross-fault can prevent a demand cannot be determined from the signal-level architecture.
hazardous_consequence: The fault can remain latent and combine with another input fault to prevent recognition of an E-stop demand; the direct consequence of the cross-fault alone is architecture-dependent.
detection_mechanism: CH-B has a stated cross-fault diagnostic expectation, but no implemented mechanism is supplied.
recommended_action: Obtain the input schematic and controller configuration, then test each credible CH-A-to-CH-B coupling against the expected diagnostic response.
assumptions: The coupling can reduce independence without itself creating a clear demand/off state.
missing_information: Input test pulses, source impedances, wiring topology and cross-fault detection coverage are not supplied.

failure_mode: A CTRL-01 input-processing failure fails to recognize demanded-state changes on both CH-A and CH-B.
local_effect: The physical inputs reach demand/off but the controller logic retains a healthy input state.
system_effect: Q1/Q2 remain energized, K1/K2 remain closed and SF-01 is lost.
hazardous_consequence: Power enabling hazardous robot motion can remain present after ESTOP-01 is pressed.
detection_mechanism: No independent in-system detection of this common controller failure is identified; a two-channel fault-injection or demand test could reveal it.
recommended_action: Obtain CTRL-01 safety behavior and configuration evidence and execute a demand test that traces physical inputs, interpreted states, outputs and contactor states.
assumptions: The input-processing failure can affect both monitored channels as a common controller failure.
missing_information: CTRL-01 internal hardware, firmware, diagnostic coverage and configuration are explicitly outside the available black-box detail.

failure_mode: CTRL-01 is configured to require both channels to indicate demand instead of responding to either channel.
local_effect: A single-channel demand/off state is treated only as a discrepancy and not as an E-stop demand.
system_effect: With one channel stuck healthy, Q1/Q2 can remain energized instead of entering the safe state, contrary to SF-01 and SR-001.
hazardous_consequence: A coincident single-channel failure and E-stop demand can leave power enabling hazardous robot motion present.
detection_mechanism: Design/configuration review and separate CH-A-only and CH-B-only demand tests.
recommended_action: Verify the controller configuration against the either-channel behavior and retain separate timestamped traces for CH-A-only and CH-B-only demands.
assumptions: CTRL-01 behavior is configurable and can be set to an incorrect channel-evaluation rule.
missing_information: The actual CTRL-01 application configuration and configuration-control evidence are not supplied.

failure_mode: A common CTRL-01 control failure leaves both Q1 and Q2 commanded energized after a correctly recognized E-stop demand.
local_effect: The controller recognizes CH-A/CH-B demand but does not issue the required de-energizing commands.
system_effect: K1 and K2 remain energized/closed and SF-01 is lost.
hazardous_consequence: Power enabling hazardous robot motion can remain present after ESTOP-01 is pressed.
detection_mechanism: A demand test comparing input-state timestamps with Q1/Q2 and K1/K2 traces; no independent runtime detector for the common output-command failure is specified.
recommended_action: Fault-inject the controller command path at the black-box boundary and verify that common failures affecting both outputs are represented in the fault matrix.
assumptions: A common controller failure can affect both output commands.
missing_information: CTRL-01 internal architecture and any independent output shutdown mechanism are not supplied.

failure_mode: CTRL-01 de-energizes Q1/Q2 later than the illustrative 100 ms target after an E-stop demand.
local_effect: The output commands remain energized beyond the stated target interval before changing to de-energized.
system_effect: SF-01 is achieved late; K1/K2 opening and drive-power removal are delayed by at least the controller-output delay plus unprovided contactor dynamics.
hazardous_consequence: Hazardous robot motion can continue longer than intended, but the safety significance cannot be decided because the 100 ms output target and 500 ms motion-cessation target are illustrative rather than validated machine limits.
detection_mechanism: Timestamped CH-A and CH-B demand-to-Q1/Q2 traces required by SR-001.
recommended_action: Measure demand-to-output and output-to-contactor timing separately and replace the illustrative target with a validated machine-specific limit before acceptance use.
assumptions: A-010 is the basis for the illustrative 100 ms target as stated in the SR-001 note.
missing_information: Validated stopping-time limit, contactor operating times, evidence against the illustrative 500 ms motion-cessation target and timing test results are not supplied.

failure_mode: Channel-discrepancy monitoring is disabled or configured with a limit exceeding the illustrative 100 ms value.
local_effect: An asynchronous or stuck-healthy input channel is not diagnosed within the stated interval.
system_effect: A demand from the other channel should still reach the safe state, but the degraded input condition can remain latent and reset may not be inhibited as required.
hazardous_consequence: No immediate hazardous consequence is expected while the remaining input channel works; an undetected loss of input independence can combine with a later fault to prevent E-stop recognition.
detection_mechanism: Negative discrepancy simulation and verification of the fault log and blocked-reset response required by SR-003.
recommended_action: Review and lock the discrepancy configuration, then test values just below and above the stated limit and retain the results.
assumptions: The discrepancy behavior and time limit are configurable in CTRL-01.
missing_information: Actual discrepancy configuration, its relationship to A-010 and validation of the 100 ms value are not supplied.

failure_mode: One safety output or its field wire fails open or remains de-energized.
local_effect: The corresponding K1 or K2 coil de-energizes and its contactor opens while the other path can remain commanded closed.
system_effect: Because K1 and K2 are assumed to be series contactors and one opening contactor removes drive power, the system enters the safe state but loses availability and one de-energization path.
hazardous_consequence: No continued hazardous motion is expected from this single fault under the series-path assumption; unintended power removal can occur.
detection_mechanism: The supplied evidence specifies output diagnostics plus EDM, but detection of a contactor that fails to close during normal operation is not defined.
recommended_action: Open-circuit each output and field wire separately and verify contactor, drive-power, EDM and reset behavior.
assumptions: A-006 is the series-path assumption referenced by SR-005.
One correctly opening contactor is sufficient to remove drive power.
missing_information: Output circuit schematic and monitoring of contactor closure are not supplied.

failure_mode: One safety output or its field wire is stuck energized, including a single short-to-24 V fault.
local_effect: The corresponding K1 or K2 coil remains energized and that contactor remains closed on demand.
system_effect: The other independently controlled contactor should open and remove drive power; the safe state is achieved in a degraded condition, and EDM or output diagnostics should inhibit reset.
hazardous_consequence: No immediate hazardous consequence is expected for this single fault under the series-path assumption; a later failure of the remaining opening path could cause loss of SF-01.
detection_mechanism: Output diagnostics and EDM mismatch, verified by the short-to-24 V and stuck-output tests in SR-010.
recommended_action: Inject the energized fault separately on Q1 and Q2, confirm that the other contactor removes power and verify fault detection and reset inhibition.
assumptions: A-006 is the series-path assumption referenced by SR-005.
The unaffected output and contactor operate correctly.
missing_information: Actual output diagnostic coverage and short-to-24 V behavior are not supplied.

failure_mode: A common field-wiring fault or backfeed keeps both K1 and K2 coils energized after Q1/Q2 are commanded de-energized.
local_effect: Both contactor coils remain powered independently of the commanded E-stop output state.
system_effect: K1 and K2 remain closed, drive power is not removed and SF-01 is lost.
hazardous_consequence: Hazardous robot motion can continue during the E-stop demand.
detection_mechanism: EDM should report that the contactors have not opened, but detection occurs after failure of the demanded power-removal action and does not itself remove the backfeed.
recommended_action: Review the field-wiring schematic for common energizing sources and inject the credible common backfeed while tracing Q1/Q2, coil, main-contact and EDM states.
assumptions: A common electrical source or coupling can energize both coils downstream of the independent outputs.
missing_information: The output and field-wiring schematic, protective elements and routing are not supplied.

failure_mode: Q1 and Q2 are configured or allocated to the same physical output path instead of independent paths.
local_effect: Both logical commands depend on one physical output or shared control point.
system_effect: A single stuck-energized output fault can keep both K1 and K2 energized, defeating the intended independent-path behavior.
hazardous_consequence: The configuration defect can remain latent until an output fault coincides with an E-stop demand, at which point hazardous motion may continue.
detection_mechanism: I/O allocation and configuration review under SR-002, independent-path tracing under SR-005 and separate output fault injection.
recommended_action: Verify the physical I/O allocation and configuration records and demonstrate independent control of K1 and K2.
assumptions: CTRL-01 output allocation is configurable.
missing_information: I/O allocation, controller configuration and schematic evidence are not supplied.

failure_mode: One contactor main-contact set is welded or otherwise fails to open when its coil is de-energized.
local_effect: The affected power path remains closed while the other contactor can open.
system_effect: One correctly opening series contactor removes drive power, so SF-01 is achieved in a degraded condition; EDM should detect the failed-open contactor and inhibit reset.
hazardous_consequence: No immediate hazardous consequence is expected for this single fault under the series-path assumption; allowing reset with the fault present would leave only one effective interruption path.
detection_mechanism: EDM-01 verification of both contactors open and the K1-welded and K2-welded tests required by SR-006.
recommended_action: Inject K1-welded and K2-welded cases separately, verify drive-power removal by the other contactor and confirm that EDM blocks reset.
assumptions: A-006 is the series-path assumption referenced by SR-005.
The unaffected contactor opens correctly.
missing_information: Contactor component data and the detailed force-guided feedback circuit are not supplied.

failure_mode: One contactor coil is open circuit or the contactor mechanically fails to close when energization is requested.
local_effect: The affected contactor remains open.
system_effect: The series drive-power path remains interrupted, preventing or stopping power-enabled robot motion; system availability is lost.
hazardous_consequence: The defined safe power state is maintained; no continued hazardous motion is identified within the supplied boundary.
detection_mechanism: EDM may show the contactor open, but the supplied EDM behavior verifies opening before reset and does not specify detection of failure to close.
recommended_action: Inject coil-open and fail-to-close conditions and record drive-power, auxiliary-feedback and controller-state behavior.
assumptions: An open contactor interrupts the assumed series power path.
missing_information: Closure monitoring, normal energization sequence and contactor component behavior are not supplied.

failure_mode: A common-cause failure prevents both K1 and K2 main-contact sets from opening on demand.
local_effect: Both series power contacts remain closed although both coils are commanded de-energized.
system_effect: Neither interruption path opens, drive power remains present and SF-01 is lost.
hazardous_consequence: Hazardous robot motion can continue after ESTOP-01 is pressed.
detection_mechanism: EDM should indicate that opening was not proven, but it cannot remove drive power; a common-cause fault-injection or equivalent controlled simulation is required to expose the effect.
recommended_action: Identify credible shared causes from the real contactor installation and include applicable dual-fail-to-open cases in the human-reviewed fault matrix.
assumptions: A shared cause can prevent both nominally independent contactors from opening.
missing_information: Contactor types, installation environment, separation and common-cause analysis are not supplied.

failure_mode: The drive-power circuit is miswired so K1 and K2 are not effective independent series interruption paths, or one contactor is bypassed.
local_effect: Opening one contactor does not necessarily interrupt the power path as assumed.
system_effect: A single stuck-closed contactor or bypassed path can prevent drive-power removal on an E-stop demand, invalidating the stated single-fault behavior.
hazardous_consequence: Hazardous robot motion can continue despite one contactor opening on demand.
detection_mechanism: Schematic review, independent-path trace and power-state testing required by SR-005; EDM alone monitors auxiliary feedback and does not prove the actual power topology in the supplied model.
recommended_action: Verify the as-designed and as-tested power path against A-006 and demonstrate that opening either K1 or K2 independently removes drive power.
assumptions: A wiring or configuration error can violate the assumed series topology.
missing_information: An installation wiring diagram and physical validation results are explicitly not supplied.

failure_mode: The EDM feedback loop is open circuit or stuck in the not-ready state.
local_effect: CTRL-01 cannot obtain healthy proof that both K1 and K2 are open.
system_effect: Reset should remain inhibited even when the contactors have opened; the safe state is maintained but restart availability is lost.
hazardous_consequence: No automatic or permitted restart is expected from this fault if SR-006 and SR-008 are implemented; the consequence is failure to reset.
detection_mechanism: EDM mismatch and the resulting reset-not-ready state.
recommended_action: Open the EDM loop and verify distinct diagnostic labeling and persistent reset inhibition.
assumptions: An open EDM loop is interpreted as unhealthy/not ready by CTRL-01.
missing_information: EDM electrical polarity and detailed controller truth table are not supplied.

failure_mode: The EDM loop is shorted, bypassed or otherwise stuck in a false healthy/open-proven state.
local_effect: CTRL-01 can receive acceptable EDM feedback even when one contactor has failed to open.
system_effect: A single welded contactor can remain undetected and reset can be permitted, leaving only one effective power-interruption path for the next demand.
hazardous_consequence: The hidden degradation can combine with a later failure of the remaining contactor or output path and allow hazardous motion to continue during an E-stop demand.
detection_mechanism: No effective runtime detection is established for a plausibly valid false-healthy EDM state; EDM bypass and welded-contactor combination testing can reveal it.
recommended_action: Inject false-healthy EDM feedback with K1 welded and K2 welded separately and verify that the fault cannot permit reset unnoticed.
assumptions: An electrical EDM fault can reproduce the controller's accepted open-proven state.
missing_information: EDM wiring, signal polarity, pulse diagnostics and force-guided auxiliary-contact arrangement are not supplied.

failure_mode: RESET-01 or its input wiring is open circuit or stuck inactive.
local_effect: CTRL-01 receives no deliberate reset edge after recovery.
system_effect: Reset remains unavailable and Q1/Q2 should not be re-energized through the reset sequence; the safe state persists.
hazardous_consequence: No unintended restart is expected; system availability is lost.
detection_mechanism: A reset-sequence test shows that no reset edge is received and reset remains blocked.
recommended_action: Inject an inactive/open reset input after a valid E-stop recovery and verify that the controller remains reset-not-ready without re-energizing outputs.
missing_information: Reset input electrical topology and diagnostics are not supplied.

failure_mode: RESET-01 or its input wiring is stuck active, producing a steady level instead of a deliberate edge.
local_effect: The reset input remains continuously active.
system_effect: CTRL-01 should reject the steady level and keep reset inhibited; a new deliberate reset edge cannot be formed until the fault is cleared.
hazardous_consequence: No unintended restart is expected if the monitored-edge behavior is implemented; restart availability is lost.
detection_mechanism: The held/stuck reset negative test required by SR-008.
recommended_action: Hold RESET active through E-stop release, EDM recovery and power restoration and verify that no reset or output re-energization occurs.
assumptions: CTRL-01 implements the stated monitored rising-edge and steady-level rejection behavior.
missing_information: Actual reset configuration and test result are not supplied.

failure_mode: RESET-01 or its wiring generates an unintended rising edge after the E-stop channels and EDM feedback have become healthy.
local_effect: CTRL-01 receives an apparently valid reset edge without a deliberate operator action.
system_effect: Reset inhibition can be cleared and Q1/Q2 may become eligible for re-energization, although the supplied evidence states that reset itself must not command robot motion.
hazardous_consequence: Loss of deliberate reset can re-enable the power path, but whether hazardous robot motion follows cannot be determined because robot motion-control behavior is out of scope.
detection_mechanism: Reset-edge logging and negative testing for unintended or simulated reset edges; no runtime plausibility mechanism beyond the edge and prerequisite checks is specified.
recommended_action: Inject a spurious reset edge after recovery and verify the exact Q1/Q2 response and that reset does not command robot motion.
assumptions: A transient wiring or contact event can be interpreted as a valid rising edge.
missing_information: Post-reset output behavior, robot motion-control interlocks and reset-input filtering are not supplied.

failure_mode: CTRL-01 reset logic incorrectly accepts reset while an E-stop channel is demanded/unhealthy or EDM has not proven both contactors open.
local_effect: A reset edge bypasses one or more required reset prerequisites.
system_effect: Restart inhibition is lost and Q1/Q2 can be re-energized while the input or contactor state is unsafe or unresolved.
hazardous_consequence: Power enabling hazardous robot motion can be restored contrary to the safety function; whether motion begins immediately is unknown because reset is specified not to command motion and motion control is out of scope.
detection_mechanism: Reset-sequence negative tests covering demanded channels, channel discrepancy, unhealthy EDM and held reset as required by SR-003, SR-006 and SR-008.
recommended_action: Execute a reset truth-table test for every invalid prerequisite combination and trace reset state, Q1/Q2, K1/K2 and EDM.
assumptions: Acceptance of an invalid reset can permit Q1/Q2 re-energization.
missing_information: The implemented reset state machine and the external robot motion interlocks are not supplied.

failure_mode: SUP-01 control power is lost.
local_effect: CTRL-01 and the K1/K2 coils lose 24 V control power.
system_effect: Q1/Q2 and K1/K2 de-energize, the contactors open and the safe state is reached; restoration must not cause automatic restart.
hazardous_consequence: No continued hazardous motion is expected from the power-loss condition under the specified de-energize-to-safe behavior; unintended restart on restoration is a separate failure candidate.
detection_mechanism: Power interruption test with output and contactor state evidence during loss and after restoration.
recommended_action: Interrupt SUP-01 during normal operation and during reset recovery, then verify safe-state entry and persistent restart inhibition after restoration.
assumptions: Loss of SUP-01 actually removes power from both contactor coils as stated in the system definition.
missing_information: Stored-energy behavior and measured contactor drop-out timing are not supplied.

failure_mode: After SUP-01 restoration, CTRL-01 initializes into a reset/energized state instead of retaining restart inhibition.
local_effect: Q1/Q2 can energize without a new valid manual reset edge.
system_effect: K1/K2 can close and restore drive power automatically after control-power recovery, contrary to SR-009.
hazardous_consequence: Power enabling hazardous robot motion can be restored unexpectedly; actual motion initiation is unknown because motion-control software is out of scope.
detection_mechanism: Power interruption and restoration test with no reset action, observing Q1/Q2, K1/K2 and the reset state.
recommended_action: Test restoration from each relevant pre-loss state and verify that a fresh valid reset sequence is required before output energization is permitted.
assumptions: CTRL-01 startup behavior can be affected by application configuration or retained state.
missing_information: CTRL-01 startup-state logic, retained-memory behavior and robot motion interlocks are not supplied.

failure_mode: SUP-01 is intermittent or at an intermediate voltage that does not produce the complete de-energization assumed for a total power loss.
local_effect: CTRL-01 and the two contactor coils may not change state together or predictably.
system_effect: The evidence is insufficient to determine whether both contactors open, whether one path remains energized or how CTRL-01 initializes after recovery.
hazardous_consequence: A hazardous consequence is possible only if the supply condition keeps both power paths closed or causes uncommanded re-energization; this cannot be determined from the supplied evidence.
detection_mechanism: No voltage threshold, brownout diagnostic or intermediate-voltage behavior is specified; controlled power-profile testing could determine the response.
recommended_action: Obtain permitted voltage ranges and dropout/reset characteristics for CTRL-01, K1 and K2, then test representative controlled voltage interruptions without treating AI output as evidence.
assumptions: SUP-01 can experience a non-ideal interruption rather than a clean loss and restoration.
missing_information: Supply characteristics, load behavior, controller brownout thresholds, contactor dropout thresholds and test results are not supplied.
